schema.description: {{COMPANY_NAME}} reusable Merlino Catalogue threat-profile template for System Integrator / MSP organisations. TP-07 models Business Email Compromise, phishing, adversary-in-the-middle identity phishing, Microsoft Teams/service phishing, vishing, impersonation, device-code/OAuth token theft, browser/session takeover, mailbox persistence, internal spearphishing, SaaS collection and financial fraud. It incorporates Microsoft Q2 2026 email/Teams threat observations, current UNC6671/BlackFile identity-extortion behavior, and MITRE Kali365/ShinyHunters context while remaining a reusable actor-neutral profile. data.Name: TP-07 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Obtain leaked, infostealer-derived or previously compromised credentials for employees, executives, finance staff, help-desk personnel and administrators. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: BEC and identity-first phishing operations frequently begin with credential intelligence. For a system integrator, identities may also expose customer conversations, privileged access paths and trusted business relationships. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: Employee identities, Finance identities, Executives, Help desk, Cloud administrators. Detection opportunities: Leaked credential monitoring; Identity Protection risk signals; Credential exposure correlation. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Credential exposure response; No password reuse.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: BEC and identity-first phishing operations frequently begin with credential intelligence. For a system integrator, identities may also expose customer conversations, privileged access paths and trusted business relationships. Threat-led context: Current identity-centric extortion operations rely heavily on stolen or socially engineered credentials. Applicability=Core; Phase=Targeting; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Collect corporate email addresses for employees, executives, finance, HR, help desk, sales and technical personnel. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Email addresses are the foundation for phishing, password spraying, impersonation and thread hijacking. Professional-services organisations expose many identities through projects, events and public collaboration. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: Corporate email addresses, Privileged users, Customer-facing staff. Detection opportunities: Targeted identity intelligence; Password-spray correlation; Brand monitoring. Defensive considerations: Reduce exposure of privileged admin identifiers; Separate privileged identities.

data.Name: TP-07 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Employee Names
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Identify named employees whose role, authority or customer relationships can make a phishing pretext believable. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: BEC succeeds through trust and context. Knowing names, reporting lines and customer-facing personnel allows attackers to impersonate credible senders and target users capable of approving financial or security-sensitive actions. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: Executives, Finance, HR, Help desk, Sales, Project managers, Technical consultants. Detection opportunities: User-reported impersonation; Brand monitoring. Defensive considerations: Limit unnecessary publication of sensitive roles; Security awareness for high-risk functions.

data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Research customers, suppliers, partners, MSP relationships and other trusted business connections that can be impersonated or compromised. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Business relationships are especially valuable against a system integrator because users expect frequent external communications and may trust messages from customers, Microsoft, vendors, accountants, recruiters and project partners. Primary assets at risk: Customer relationships, Supplier relationships, Partner ecosystem, Managed-service relationships. Detection opportunities: Threat-intel monitoring for partner impersonation; Look-alike domain monitoring. Defensive considerations: Out-of-band verification for sensitive supplier/customer requests; External sender labelling.

data.Name: TP-07 | Gather Victim Org Information: Identify Roles
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Identify personnel with authority over payments, payroll, MFA reset, identity administration, support, executive decisions or customer access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Role targeting enables both classic BEC and modern identity compromise. Help-desk and privileged-role targeting can turn social engineering into tenant-wide access. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Targeting. Primary assets at risk: Finance, Payroll, Help desk, Global administrators, Executives, Customer administrators. Detection opportunities: Targeting intelligence; Repeated phishing against named roles. Defensive considerations: Role-specific awareness; Strong help-desk identity verification; Separate admin identities.

data.Name: TP-07 | Establish Accounts: Social Media Accounts

data.Description: Create social-network personas that support recruiter, colleague, customer, executive or vendor impersonation. Detection opportunities: Brand/persona monitoring; Employee reports. Defensive considerations: Verification procedures; Awareness around external persona contact.

data.Name: TP-07 | Establish Accounts: Cloud Accounts
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create cloud or collaboration accounts used to contact targets through Microsoft Teams, SaaS trials or other trusted services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cross-tenant collaboration can make attacker messages appear more legitimate than unsolicited email and may bypass traditional email security controls. Applicability: Teams / SaaS Conditional. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Persona. Primary assets at risk: Microsoft Teams, Cloud collaboration, SaaS trial tenants. Detection opportunities: External tenant contact anomalies; New external domain/tenant messaging users. Defensive considerations: Restrict external collaboration; Tenant allow/block controls; User awareness.

data.Description: Compromise an existing social-media or professional-network account and use the trusted identity to approach employees. data.Name: TP-07 | Compromise Accounts: Email Accounts

data.Description: Compromise a legitimate email account belonging to an employee, supplier, customer or business partner and use it for phishing or fraud. Detection opportunities: Impossible/unusual sign-in; New forwarding rules; Outbound phishing burst; Thread hijack anomalies. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Mailbox audit; Risk-based Conditional Access.

data.Name: TP-07 | Acquire Infrastructure: Domains

data.Description: Acquire look-alike, typosquat or brand-mimicking domains for credential harvesting, fake login portals, email sending or extortion. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Modern vishing/AiTM campaigns register convincing organisation- or SSO-themed domains. Domains may reference passkeys, enrollment, Microsoft, payroll, SharePoint or customer brands. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Phishing Infrastructure. Primary assets at risk: Corporate brand, SSO login, Customer/vendor brands. Detection opportunities: Domain registration monitoring; Homoglyph/typosquat detection; Certificate transparency monitoring. Defensive considerations: Defensive domain registration; Brand monitoring; Web filtering.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. data.Name: TP-07 | Acquire Infrastructure: Web Services
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Register or use legitimate web services to host lures, redirects, phishing pages, documents or campaign infrastructure. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Trusted services such as cloud hosting, document platforms and link services help phishing bypass simple reputation filtering and blend with ordinary traffic. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Phishing Infrastructure. Primary assets at risk: Cloud web services, File-sharing platforms, URL services. Detection opportunities: Rare web service domains in email; New SaaS redirect chains. Defensive considerations: Safe Links; Web filtering; URL detonation.

data.Description: Install valid TLS certificates on attacker-controlled phishing or AiTM infrastructure. data.Name: TP-07 | Stage Capabilities: Link Target
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Stage malicious link targets using masked URLs, redirects, link shorteners, trusted SaaS domains or one-time URLs. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Link-target staging supports modern email, QR-code and Teams phishing while making destination analysis harder. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Prepare Phishing Infrastructure. Primary assets at risk: Email links, QR-code redirects, Teams links, Credential portals. Detection opportunities: URL-chain analysis; Newly registered domains; Redirector reputation. Defensive considerations: URL rewriting/detonation; Browser protection; Web filtering.

data.Description: Send forms, HTML files or documents designed to make a victim disclose credentials or other sensitive information rather than directly execute malware. Defensive considerations: Attachment sandboxing; Safe Attachments; User awareness.

data.Name: TP-07 | Phishing for Information: Spearphishing Voice

data.Description: Call employees while impersonating IT, help desk, customer support or another trusted role to elicit credentials, MFA codes or security information. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Vishing is a major 2026 identity threat. Attackers deliberately use personal phones and urgent passkey/MFA migration pretexts to evade enterprise communication controls. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Social Engineering. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Help-desk verification; No credential/MFA disclosure by phone.

data.Name: TP-07 | Social Engineering: Impersonation
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Impersonate an executive, finance officer, help-desk analyst, Microsoft support representative, customer or supplier. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: ATT&CK explicitly links impersonation to BEC and financial fraud. System integrators have dense external trust relationships, making customer/vendor impersonation especially credible. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Social Engineering. Primary assets at risk: Finance, Help desk, Executives, Customer-facing staff. Detection opportunities: Display-name impersonation; User reports; Behavior/context anomaly. Defensive considerations: Out-of-band verification; Payment controls; Help-desk identity proofing.

data.Name: TP-07 | Social Engineering: Email Spoofing
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Manipulate sender identity or email headers so messages appear to originate from an internal user, executive, supplier or trusted domain. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Email spoofing remains important where SPF/DKIM/DMARC or complex mail routing is weak or misconfigured. It can support payment fraud without needing an account takeover. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Delivery / Stealth. Primary assets at risk: Corporate domain, Supplier/customer domains, Email recipients. Detection opportunities: SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures; Composite authentication anomalies; Direct Send anomalies. Defensive considerations: DMARC enforcement; SPF/DKIM; Secure mail routing; External sender labelling.

data.Name: TP-07 | Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Send PDF, Office, HTML or other attachments that deliver malware, redirect to phishing pages, display QR codes or start a social-engineering flow. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Attachments remain useful because they can carry branded content and hide final destinations from simple URL inspection. Kali365 has delivered Office/PDF attachments that direct victims to actor-controlled landing pages. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: Email, User endpoint, Browser. Detection opportunities: Attachment detonation; Office child process; QR/HTML attachment detection. Defensive considerations: Safe Attachments; Block risky formats; EDR.

data.Name: TP-07 | Phishing: Spearphishing Link
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Send email or message links leading to AiTM proxies, credential portals, device-code flows, malware or fake support pages. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is the primary link-delivery TTP for Entra/M365 phishing. QR-code phishing also ultimately drives the victim to a malicious URL and is represented here when delivered as a link/redirect flow. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: Email, Teams, Browser, Entra identity. Detection opportunities: URL click telemetry; Redirect chain; Newly registered domain; AiTM landing page. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Safe Links; Browser protection.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | User Execution: Malicious Link
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Rely on the user to open a malicious link that starts credential capture, device authorization, malware download or remote-support abuse. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: User interaction remains the handoff between delivery and identity compromise in many phishing campaigns. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: User Interaction. Primary assets at risk: Browser, Entra identity, Endpoint. Detection opportunities: Email/Teams click followed by risky sign-in; Browser to newly registered domain. Defensive considerations: Safe Links; Browser isolation/protection; User training.

data.Name: TP-07 | User Execution: Malicious Copy and Paste
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Trick the victim into copying/pasting a device code or command as part of a fake authentication, CAPTCHA, support or remediation flow. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: ATT&CK now maps Kali365 device-code authorization to this technique. Social engineering can cause the user to complete a legitimate authorization flow that grants attacker-controlled token access. Applicability: Current 2026. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: User Interaction / Authentication. Primary assets at risk: Browser, Device-code login, PowerShell/Run dialog, Entra identity. Detection opportunities: Device-code authentication after phishing; Clipboard-to-shell chain; Unusual device authorization. Defensive considerations: Block/restrict device-code auth where appropriate; Phishing-resistant MFA; User training.

data.Name: TP-07 | Remote Access Tools: Remote Desktop Software
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Persuade a victim to install or enable Quick Assist, AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, TeamViewer or similar remote-support software. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Support impersonation can convert a social-engineering conversation directly into interactive endpoint control using legitimate tools that may already be trusted. Applicability: Vishing / Support Impersonation. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Initial Foothold. Primary assets at risk: User endpoint, Remote support tooling, Administrative session. Detection opportunities: New RMM installation; Quick Assist after external Teams call; Remote session outside support workflow. Defensive considerations: Application allow-list; Verified support procedures; Session logging.

data.Description: Proxy the victim's authentication interaction to the legitimate identity provider while intercepting credentials, MFA and session artifacts. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Token protection; Conditional Access.

data.Name: TP-07 | Browser Session Hijacking

data.Description: Capture or hijack browser session state and replay it in attacker infrastructure. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Modern phishing kits provide affiliates with session-replay capabilities, reducing reliance on passwords and enabling authenticated access after MFA. Detection opportunities: Session use from different device/IP; Cookie/session replay patterns. Defensive considerations: Token protection; Managed device requirements; Rapid session revocation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Steal Web Session Cookie
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Capture session cookies or equivalent web authentication artifacts during phishing/AiTM activity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Stolen cookies may provide immediate authenticated access and can bypass the need to repeat MFA. Applicability: AiTM Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Session Theft. Primary assets at risk: FedAuth/session cookies, M365, Entra, SaaS. Detection opportunities: Cookie reuse from new device/IP; Session anomaly after phishing. Defensive considerations: Token protection; Continuous Access Evaluation; Rapid revocation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Stolen cookies may provide immediate authenticated access and can bypass the need to repeat MFA. Threat-led context: Kali365 captures session cookies; UNC6671 reuses FedAuth-style sessions for SaaS access. Applicability=AiTM Core; Phase=Session Theft; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Steal Application Access Token
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Capture OAuth access/refresh tokens via AiTM, device-code authorization, malicious OAuth flow or compromised session. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Access tokens can provide Graph/M365/SaaS access without the user's password and are central to modern Microsoft 365 phishing-as-a-service. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Token Theft. Primary assets at risk: OAuth access token, Refresh token, Microsoft Graph, M365. Detection opportunities: Token use from unusual client/IP; Device-code auth anomalies; Consent/token issuance after phishing. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Restrict device-code auth where appropriate; Token revocation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Replay an authenticated web-session cookie to access M365 or SaaS resources. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Session replay can continue until the token/session is invalidated and may appear to be an already authenticated user session. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Post-Compromise Access. Primary assets at risk: M365, Entra admin portals, SaaS. Detection opportunities: New IP/device for existing session; Impossible/atypical travel. Defensive considerations: Session protection; Managed-device requirements; Rapid revocation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Session replay can continue until the token/session is invalidated and may appear to be an already authenticated user session. Threat-led context: UNC6671 reused valid session cookies to access SharePoint/OneDrive. Applicability=Core; Phase=Post-Compromise Access; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. It intentionally includes both classic BEC and modern identity-first phishing that may never deploy malware. Generic Entra identity compromise is expanded in TP-01, privileged-access compromise in TP-04, ransomware impact in TP-06 and full SaaS/data-theft extortion in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation

data.Description: Generate repeated MFA prompts or synchronize a vishing interaction with MFA requests to induce approval. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: ATT&CK explicitly notes combining spearphishing voice with MFA request generation. Help-desk pretexts make unexpected MFA activity appear legitimate. Detection opportunities: Repeated MFA prompts; Denied/expired requests; Prompt immediately after external call. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Number matching; User education.

data.Name: TP-07 | Brute Force: Password Spraying

data.Description: Attempt common passwords across known corporate email identities. Defensive considerations: MFA; Smart lockout; Password protection.

data.Name: TP-07 | Brute Force: Credential Stuffing
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Try previously breached credentials against email, cloud and collaboration services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Credential stuffing can produce the initial mailbox compromise later used for BEC, internal spearphishing or thread hijacking. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Credential Acquisition. Primary assets at risk: M365, Entra, SaaS. Detection opportunities: Leaked credential detections; Unfamiliar sign-ins. Defensive considerations: MFA; Unique credentials; Leak monitoring.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Credential stuffing can produce the initial mailbox compromise later used for BEC, internal spearphishing or thread hijacking. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to phishing/BEC/AiTM/social-engineering operations. Applicability=Core; Phase=Credential Acquisition; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use the compromised cloud identity to access mailbox, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and connected SaaS applications. Detection opportunities: SigninLogs; Risk detections; Unusual mailbox/SaaS activity. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Conditional Access; Risk-based session controls.

data.Name: TP-07 | Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create inbox or transport forwarding rules that send copies of incoming email to attacker-controlled addresses. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Forwarding provides persistent intelligence on invoices, customer conversations and incident response even after direct access becomes risky. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Mailbox Persistence / Collection. Primary assets at risk: Exchange Online mailbox, Finance mail, Customer communications. Detection opportunities: New-InboxRule/Set-InboxRule; External forwarding; Transport-rule change. Defensive considerations: Disable unnecessary external forwarding; Audit rules; Alert on forwarding.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. data.Name: TP-07 | Hide Artifacts: Email Hiding Rules

Defensive considerations: Mailbox-rule audit; Alert on delete/move rules for security keywords.

data.Name: TP-07 | Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Add weaker factors, remove MFA requirements or alter authentication methods to preserve account access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Controlling the victim's authentication methods makes password resets less effective and can protect attacker persistence. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Identity Persistence. Primary assets at risk: MFA methods, Authentication policy, Compromised identity. Detection opportunities: MFA method add/remove/reset; Privileged authentication policy change. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Strong identity proofing; Alert on auth-method changes.

data.Name: TP-07 | Cloud Application Integration

data.Description: Create, consent to or abuse an OAuth/cloud application with mailbox, files or directory permissions. Detection opportunities: New app registration; Admin/user consent; High-risk scopes. Defensive considerations: Restrict user consent; Admin consent workflow; App governance.

data.Name: TP-07 | Create Account: Cloud Account
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Create an additional cloud identity after obtaining administrative access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A separate identity provides persistence and can later receive mailbox delegation or cloud roles. Applicability: Privileged Compromise. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Entra ID, M365. Detection opportunities: New account outside lifecycle process; Account immediately assigned rights. Defensive considerations: Identity governance; Alert on admin-created accounts.

data.Name: TP-07 | Account Discovery: Email Account
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Enumerate email accounts, mailboxes and the global address list. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mailbox discovery identifies executives, finance users, administrators and new phishing targets. ATT&CK updated this technique on 4 August 2026 and maps Kali365 mailbox enumeration to it. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Post-Compromise Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Exchange Online, Global Address List, Mailboxes. Detection opportunities: Get-GlobalAddressList; Graph mailbox enumeration; Bulk directory queries. Defensive considerations: Monitor unusual mailbox enumeration; Behavior analytics.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Mailbox discovery identifies executives, finance users, administrators and new phishing targets. ATT&CK updated this technique on 4 August 2026 and maps Kali365 mailbox enumeration to it. Threat-led context: Kali365 uses Graph to enumerate mailboxes. Applicability=BEC Core; Phase=Post-Compromise Discovery; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Cloud Service Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Identify SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, CRM and other cloud services reachable through the compromised SSO identity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Modern identity-extortion operations quickly pivot from one account into connected SaaS data sources. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Post-Compromise Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Microsoft 365, CRM, Ticketing, Cloud storage. Detection opportunities: New SaaS applications accessed after risky login. Defensive considerations: Least privilege; Conditional Access; SaaS monitoring.

data.Name: TP-07 | Internal Spearphishing
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use a compromised employee mailbox or collaboration account to send phishing or fraudulent requests to other internal users. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Internal messages inherit organisational trust and may bypass reputation-based filtering. They can target finance, help desk, administrators or customer-facing teams. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Internal Propagation. Primary assets at risk: Internal email, Teams, Employees. Detection opportunities: Outbound burst from compromised user; Internal link phishing; Thread anomalies. Defensive considerations: Internal email security; User reporting; Risk-triggered account containment.

data.Name: TP-07 | Remote Services: Cloud Services
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use SSO and valid session/token access to move from email into SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, CRM or other SaaS applications. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: A mailbox compromise often becomes broader SaaS compromise without any endpoint malware. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Cloud Lateral Movement. Primary assets at risk: M365, SaaS, Cloud applications. Detection opportunities: Cross-service activity correlation; New service access by compromised user. Defensive considerations: Conditional Access; Least privilege; SaaS monitoring.

data.Name: TP-07 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript/JScript
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use JavaScript in phishing pages to detect browser state, manage device-code flows, evade automation and coordinate token capture. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Modern phishing kits behave like full web applications. Kali365 uses JavaScript to detect sessions, manipulate device-code interaction and poll attacker infrastructure. Applicability: PhaaS / AiTM. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Phishing Page Execution. Primary assets at risk: Browser, Phishing page, Device-code flow. Detection opportunities: Malicious page script behavior; Obfuscated JS on look-alike domain. Defensive considerations: Web filtering; Browser protection.

data.Name: TP-07 | Email Collection: Remote Email Collection
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Access Exchange Online or another remote mailbox using compromised credentials, session cookies, tokens, delegation or OAuth. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Email is the core intelligence source for BEC: invoices, customers, internal processes, security alerts and existing trusted threads can all be harvested. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: Exchange Online, Executive mail, Finance mail, Customer correspondence. Detection opportunities: MailItemsAccessed; Graph/EWS mailbox reads; Unusual admin mailbox access. Defensive considerations: Mailbox audit; Least privilege; App permission governance.

data.Name: TP-07 | Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Search compromised mailboxes, attachments and cloud files for passwords, API keys, recovery phrases or other credentials. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mailboxes and project documents often contain operational secrets. Kali365 is explicitly documented searching compromised mailboxes for credential material. Applicability: Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Credential Expansion. Primary assets at risk: Email, Attachments, OneDrive, SharePoint. Detection opportunities: Search/download patterns for secret-related keywords; Access to credential documents. Defensive considerations: Secrets hygiene; DLP; No credentials in email.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Threat-led context: Kali365 searches compromised mailboxes for seed phrases and API keys. Applicability=Core; Phase=Credential Expansion; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Download files from OneDrive or other cloud storage using valid user/session access. data.Name: TP-07 | Proxy
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use reverse proxies or relay services between the victim and legitimate authentication services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: AiTM phishing infrastructure depends on proxying legitimate login traffic while retaining control of the client-facing session. ATT&CK maps Kali365 to Proxy. Applicability: AiTM Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Phishing Infrastructure / C2. Primary assets at risk: AiTM infrastructure, SSO login. Detection opportunities: Reverse-proxy fingerprints; Cloudflare/hosting infrastructure correlated with phishing domain. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Web filtering; Threat intelligence.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-07 | Generic System Integrator / MSP BEC, phishing, AiTM and social-engineering profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Applicability=AiTM Core; Phase=Phishing Infrastructure / C2; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-07 models pre-attack target research, attacker persona/infrastructure preparation, BEC and impersonation, email/Teams/vishing delivery, credential harvesting, adversary-in-the-middle authentication, OAuth/session/token theft, MFA abuse, mailbox/cloud-account takeover, mailbox persistence, email collection, internal spearphishing, SaaS pivot, data theft and financial fraud. This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Transfer stolen email, documents or SaaS exports to attacker-controlled cloud storage. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: BEC can evolve into data-theft extortion, especially in current ShinyHunters/UNC6671-style operations. Applicability: Follow-on Extortion. Detection opportunities: Large external upload; Cloud storage destination after mass download. Defensive considerations: DLP; CASB; Egress monitoring.

data.Name: TP-07 | Financial Theft
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Use impersonation or compromised business email to induce fraudulent payments, payroll changes, gift-card purchases or other transfers. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is the core impact technique for classic BEC. ATT&CK explicitly links impersonation and social engineering to financial theft. Applicability: BEC Core. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Fraud / Impact. Primary assets at risk: Accounts payable, Payroll, Corporate funds, Payment process. Detection opportunities: New beneficiary/payment detail; Urgent executive payment request; Payroll account change. Defensive considerations: Dual approval; Call-back verification; No payment-detail changes by email alone.

This record is threat-profile intelligence, not evidence that the behaviour occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-07 | Account Access Removal
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-07 BEC / Phishing / AiTM / Social Engineering
data.Description: Change passwords, authentication methods or account state to deny legitimate users access after compromise. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Lockout may extend attacker dwell time and impede rapid mailbox recovery, especially after the attacker registers their own authentication method. Applicability: Privileged Account Takeover. Phishing/BEC lifecycle phase: Response Inhibition. Primary assets at risk: Victim account, Help-desk recovery, Administrator access. Detection opportunities: Password/MFA changes followed by failed legitimate login; Account disable/reset. Defensive considerations: Emergency access; Identity recovery process; Alert on auth-method changes.
